arguments.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Asset type: fully drawn one-scene storyboard rough for Neet & Buddy Chronicles, not finished art. Landscape on warm ivory, simple clean monochrome contour pencil with smooth unhatched body interiors, fully drawn actual dogs and setting, not diagram or stick figures. Single scene, no collage, no lettering. Restrained observational editorial humor, no exaggerated cartoon anatomy. Show connected neck, shoulder, spine, ribcage, pelvis, four owned limbs, credible floor support and coherent occlusion. Neet is tan/golden-fawn with a very short SMOOTH coat, cream muzzle/chin and irregular chest bib, modest rounded head, projecting tapering muzzle, huge broad-rooted cupped triangular ears, fine long legs below a full narrow torso, a tiny near-flush rump nub only. No long tail, shag, high white socks, black saddle, giant eyes or puppy head. Buddy has a full moderately elongated continuous charcoal close-coated torso, deep chest, visible neck and genuine leg clearance on substantial legs. Modest projecting muzzle, cream moustache/beard, light curved brows, tan chest fields flanking dark throat, pale lower legs/feet, softly pendant ears. No floor-length body shag, square generic terrier, dachshund-short legs or oversized head. Human appearances if visible are provisional story design, no claimed likeness. Actual selected original photographs govern only visible anatomy; generated model supplies provisional pen/wash style, never anatomy authority. Uncalibrated photos establish no fixed proportions/relative scale, weight, ancestry, motion timing, psychology or exact palette. N35 excludes anatomy; B08 styling only and not used; B25 unavailable; B30 supplemental resting evidence only and not used. Multiple encodings of one exposure count once. B04/B24 one exposure, only B04 here. Do not copy photo backgrounds. No costume/collar/extra objects unless specified by actual scene. Draw clear contour/support construction and complete room staging for inspection.
Draw a MONOCHROME staging rough, no watercolor finish yet. Body coats smooth with no long fur hatching; only Buddy face and ears furnished.
Actual scene S049: Veterinary lobby entrance threshold seen low at a slight diagonal. Neet has recognized the disinfectant smell and is pivoting back toward the open glass door, forebody turned with attached spine/pelvis and clearly owned four fine limbs, rearfoot skidding slightly but no impossible twisted torso. Buddy calmly continues toward reception cookie jar visible on counter in background, hopeful eyes looking UP at jar, full elongated body below. Two leashes attach to simple visible comfortable collars at LOWER neck with rings/clips properly joined, leash paths clear of ears and limbs, leading to cropped adult hands outside upper frame. No clinical procedure or needle. Glass door open and doorframe defines change of mind; tile floor supports every paw. Comedy: abrupt retreat versus cookie optimism.
Input roles: Image1 N19: Neet side body, fine legs, full trunk, near-flush nub; head turned/far legs overlap. Image2 N29: Neet frontal standing chest and legs; foreshortened body, tail hidden. Image3 B29: Buddy lateral torso and tail, blurred stride; no neutral ratios/timing. Image4 B04: Buddy tidy photographed face/ears, chest and substantial legs; grass hides toes, torso foreshortened. Image5: reviewed smooth finish calibration-v004, style only. Match the photographed grooming state specified by the selected Buddy reference; no inferred new anatomy.
ROUGH COAT DRAWING RULE: use clean continuous anatomical outlines and EMPTY SMOOTH interior body planes. Do not shade Neet or Buddy torso/legs with fur hatch lines. No hairy/sawtooth outlines on neck, back, belly or tail. Only Buddy face/ear furnishings can have strands. Fully draw volume with broad simple light tone, not individual hairs.
